REJECT: problematic step claim. Verified splitAngle zero-branch (150-155), prepareCircuit_firstColumn (275-308), normalized_sum_sq (311-317); sha256 matches. Part (i) (zero sibling pair = vanishing subtree, angle zero canonical, per-split identity passes through zero norm) is CORRECT. Part (ii)/r4 is MATHEMATICALLY WRONG for the cited node: it states the minimal honest hypothesis for the whole-vector normalized first-column claim allows 'individual entries ... zero or NEGATIVE', but prepareCircuit_firstColumn carries a load-bearing hypothesis nonneg : for all b, 0 <= f b. The base case (n=0, lines 280-289) derives hf : 0 < f b and uses Real.sqrt_sq (le_of_lt hf); a single negative entry gives f(b)/sqrt(f(b)^2)=f(b)/|f(b)|=-1 != 1 (empty circuit emits amplitude 1), so negatives genuinely break the cited theorem. The item is internally contradictory: its own unresolved_issues admits 'prepareCircuit_firstColumn, which assumes nonnegativity'. Core is also a recombination of sp-001 (zero-branch) + sp-006 (strict-positivity normalization) with no genuinely new verified mathematics; the one novel assertion (negatives allowed) is false. existing_view relative to sp-001/sp-006.
